correctness.rationale: Lifting across the seam yields the stated neighbor equations even at n=3. Adding gives a three-periodic sequence with period sum two, and subtracting gives a difference recurrence whose third shift negates it. The (2,0,0) column sums force a rung pattern; a zero followed by two singleton columns forces those two bits to have equal nonzero difference, followed in three columns by the opposite sign. This proves exactly the listed words, with genuine periods three and six. The first three columns determine the lift, so finite restriction creates no phase collision and the seam gives the claimed reversal. Counting incidences yields size 2n/3. The frozen partition table is also correct: exact covers of the graph by codes recover the six explicit triples wherever all nine codes occur; with only rung patterns there is exactly one triple. Independent check 1 in /workspace/independent_checks.py tested 26 graph profiles and recovered the six explicit triples for five width/boundary pairs. The replacement python3 /workspace/repairs/1/CHECK.py passed all 26 full-code-set comparisons using neighborhood exact covers; neither check substitutes for the proof.

evidence: The Cartesian-prism theorem and its cycle case give existence, including the 3-divisibility criterion. The balanced-coloring theorems give existence for their ranges. Dejter constructs a partition of the divisible-by-three Möbius ladders. Wang et al. focus on (0,k)-regular sets rather than enumerating (1,1)-regular sets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence and explicit examples do not exhaust all arrangements of the selected bits. The broader prism criterion does not enumerate framed phases in both seam types.

evidence: Projecting the catalogued 36 strip colorings to one color gives a list of codes occurring in partitions, not a proof that an arbitrary code is on the list.

The independent equations on two selected bits force the missing exhaustion: all individual codes have three-periodic column sums with entries (2,0,0) or (0,1,1), and in the singleton case the two consecutive nonzero signs coincide then reverse after three.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim does not follow by dividing a count or renaming a color. It relies on the unconditioned binary classification, which the inspected partition and existence statements do not provide.
